column1:
The FOMC statement points to a supportive macro backdrop—solid job gains, low unemployment, inflation near 2 percent, and a transitory Q1 growth slowdown—with an accommodative stance and balanced near-term risks. Incorporating the Beige Book tilts that optimism modestly lower. District reports indicate overall activity increased and manufacturing continued to expand, but labor shortages are restraining growth in manufacturing, transportation, and construction, freight shipment growth has slowed, and consumer spending is uneven across districts. In addition, input cost pressures are feeding into selling prices, suggesting some firming inflation pressures even as core readings softened in March. Layered on top of the SLOOS evidence of somewhat tighter credit intermediation (notably in autos and CRE), the Beige Book mix implies a still-constructive outlook but with more pronounced supply-side and distribution headwinds than the FOMC tone alone suggests. On net, slightly more cautious than before.
